turn_text: On this episode of the Wise Council Project, we conclude our interview with Georgia Governor Nathan Deal. Join us as Governor Deal provides Wise Council to men and women of faith. Just attended an all-pro dad's conference where Coach Tony Dungee was there, talking to fathers about having them step up to be the leaders in the household. What do you think we can do in Georgia to encourage the dads to be there so we can prevent the kids from going into the juvenile justice system to start with?

Well, that is one of those problems that has been a huge contributor to drop out rates in our high schools and to increases in certain categories in our prison population is that they have not had a father figure in the home. And I appreciate what Tony Dungy and others are doing to try to increase that participation rate by fathers in their children's lives, not just boys, but girls as well. children need father figures and sometimes that is the missing element. As we see the number of outer birth wedlocks occurring we see that percentage of absent fathers continue to grow and we need to reverse that trend.

turn_text: That's great advice. One final question for my governor. When all said and done, what do you want your legacy to be?

Well, you know, I've never been one of those that thought a lot about a legacy. I think if you do what's right and you confront issues and don't run away from them, I believe that will be the greatest legacy you can have. I do believe, however, that the programs that we put in place during my administration of focusing education on employment, of making sure that children and parents who spend a lot of money getting their children to go to college and get degrees, are going to be an area where jobs are available in Georgia. and that they don't have to leave our state in order to get a job. That keeps families together. It allows grandparents to see their grandchildren when their children have not had to move out of the state. I think my legacy also will be the fact that I have a caring heart. I take on issues that many people say are not important. that they're not politically correct. I was told, when I announced I was going to take on criminal justice reform, that that was a risky thing for a Republican governor to do. My answer was, but it's the right thing to do. If you do the right thing, the politics will take care of itself. That's exactly what's happening. We passed in two separate years major criminal justice reform without a single descending vote in the House of the Senate. The third leg passed with only three descending votes which is virtually a unanimous vote. I believe if you're on the right side of issues that's the best legacy that you can ever have.
